clue.text: Chap Heath perhaps really wanted

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man or fellow
Edward Heath, the British prime minister, was widely known as Ted, so Heath is an example of a Ted

explanation.surface: A remark about a man resembling the politician Heath, who was much desired.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath was UK prime minister 1970-74 and always called Ted; 'perhaps' marks him as one example of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: To covet is to long for something greatly, so a thing coveted was strongly desired.

clue.text: Finale of music, and organ's stuck

indicators.note: a finale is the closing part, so only the last letter of music is used

parts.note: a lung is one of the body's organs

explanation.surface: The end of a piece of music, with an organ stuck on a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the instrument, which suits 'music', but it is the body part; 'Finale of' takes the last letter of 'music'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clung is the past tense of cling, to hold fast or adhere, which is being stuck.

clue.text: They may be smaller than one, but still to be reckoned with

definitions.text: They may be smaller than one, but still to be reckoned with

parts.words: They may be smaller than one, but still to be reckoned with
parts.note: reads like praise of small but formidable people; in fact it describes numbers written as one figure over another, often less than one, that you calculate with

explanation.surface: Small people who must nevertheless be taken seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be reckoned with' means both formidable and, literally, used in reckoning or arithmetic; a fraction like 3/4 is smaller than one.
explanation.definitionFit: Common fractions such as one half are often less than a whole number and are used in calculations.

clue.text: Run down track round outskirts of Dolgellau

indicators.note: round signals that one piece goes around another

parts.note: to track someone is to trace them

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges, so the first and last letters of Dolgellau

explanation.surface: Someone running down a track that loops around the edge of a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: Dolgellau is a town in Wales; its first and last letters D and U go inside TRACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To traduce someone is to slander them, which is to run them down.

clue.text: From the east, a wise man, almost naked, holding silver garment

indicators.note: read from the east means right to left, so the whole assembly is turned backwards
holding signals that the silver goes inside the other letters

parts.note: a seer is a prophet or wise man

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: naked means nude
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: One of the Magi arriving from the east, nearly undressed, clutching silver and a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From the east' is a reversal signal that suits the Magi of the surface; it turns the whole assembly, so the wise man ends up last in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are overalls, a piece of clothing with a bib and trousers.

clue.text: Dismiss some staff, OK? Captain backtracking

indicators.note: backtracking means the letters are read in the opposite direction
some means only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A captain asks whether cutting a few staff is acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes FFOKCAP from 'staFF OK CAPtain' and 'backtracking' reads it the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone packing is to get rid of them abruptly, which is dismissing them.

clue.text: Father to trim round end of beard

indicators.note: round signals that one piece encloses another

parts.note: to pare is to trim or cut away

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of beard

explanation.surface: A priest trimming his beard.
explanation.walkthrough: PARE goes round D, the last letter of 'beard'.
explanation.definitionFit: A padre is a chaplain, and priests are addressed as Father.

clue.text: Say the Derby cricket club admits young female international

indicators.note: admits signals that the club lets other letters inside it

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A cricket club at Derby lets in a young woman who plays for her country.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is an English horse race and one of the five 'classics' of the flat-racing season, so 'Say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The five classics are the major English flat races, the Derby among them.

clue.text: When working no idle personage he

definitions.text: When working no idle personage he

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are put to work in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone who in their working life was never an idle person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges NO IDLE PERSONAGE; the whole clue describes a retired man who was busy when employed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pensioner of old age is a retired person drawing a state pension after working life.

clue.text: Diagram shows duck C and okra pulp, oddly, A IVIE IN R in quiche

annotationWithheld.clue: Diagram shows duck C and okra pulp, oddly, A IVIE IN R in quiche

clue.text: Ignorant, lacking guidance about composer

indicators.note: about signals that one piece is placed around another

parts.note: unled means not led, without guidance
Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia

explanation.surface: An ignorant person, without direction, talking about a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the composer inside the word for unguided, splitting it before its last letter; Thomas Arne was an 18th-century English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone untaught lacks knowledge and so is ignorant.

clue.text: Translated Ouida: sound reproduction

indicators.note: translated suggests the name is turned into a different form, rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: A translation of the novelist Ouida, recorded as an audiobook.
explanation.walkthrough: Ouida was a Victorian novelist; 'Translated' rearranges her pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio refers to recorded or transmitted sound and its playback.

clue.text: A gnarled guru sat spinning — it's rather sweet

indicators.note: spinning suggests the letters are whirled into a new order

explanation.surface: An old, wizened guru sat whirling round, which is charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' rearranges all fifteen letters of A GNARLED GURU SAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Table sugar in fine crystals is sweet to taste, so 'rather sweet' describes it.

clue.text: Search for gun

explanation.definitionFit: To rifle is to ransack or go through thoroughly; a rifle is a long-barrelled firearm.

clue.text: Cut back on drink, in R theory

parts.note: to ration is to limit or cut back supply
ale is a kind of beer, a drink

explanation.surface: Someone resolving, in principle at least, to drink less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' and 'in' are linking words; the printed stray 'R' is an OCR artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying reasoning or justification, the theory behind something.

clue.text: Work (with lapis) cope belonging to bishops

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or reshape it, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bishop's cope embroidered with lapis lazuli.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' rearranges LAPIS and COPE; a cope is a long cloak worn by clergy, which makes the surface episcopal itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Episcopal means relating to or governed by bishops.

clue.text: Without any explanation, new lino's M N blue

indicators.note: new suggests making something fresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of lino's, the possessive s counting here
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone puzzled why their new linoleum floor is blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges LINOS and BLUE; the stray 'M N' is an OCR artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: A problem that cannot be solved has no explanation to be found.

clue.text: Instructs last two of students, making cases

parts.note: to instruct is to teach

indicators.note: takes the final pair of letters from students

explanation.surface: A teacher instructing the final pair of pupils in making cases.
explanation.walkthrough: TEACHES plus TS, the last two letters of 'students'; a tea chest is a wooden packing box once used to ship tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea chests are wooden boxes, often reused as packing crates for moving house.

clue.text: Area where runner ETCHES E receives medical treatment

indicators.note: the runner takes the treatment into itself, so its letters go around

parts.note: a hare is a fast runner
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy

explanation.surface: A place where an athlete gets attention from doctors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' is the hare, not an athlete; ECT (electroconvulsive therapy) goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hectare is a metric unit of land measure, 10,000 square metres.

clue.text: Gun missing new clergyman

indicators.note: missing signals that a letter is taken away

parts.note: a cannon is a large gun

explanation.surface: A clergyman whose gun has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops one N from CANNON.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a member of the clergy attached to a cathedral chapter.

clue.text: Reckoned editor supports titled chap

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the other one

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman, a man with a title

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor backs an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'supports' puts ED below COUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Counted is the past tense of count, to total up, which is to reckon.

clue.text: US political lion corrupt? There are two ways of looking at it

definitions.text: There are two ways of looking at it

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A powerful American politician accused of corruption, with debate over how to see it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges US POLITICAL LION; the definition describes an image that can be seen two ways, like the duck-rabbit drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: A visual trick image can be perceived in two different ways, deceiving the eye.

clue.text: Loaded, and left port

parts.note: Aden is a port city in Yemen

explanation.surface: A ship loaded up and left harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means carrying a heavy load, that is weighed down with cargo.

clue.text: She has an uncle that is 100 in Northumberland

indicators.note: in signals that the letters go inside the region's abbreviation

parts.note: Northumberland is in north-east England, abbreviated NE
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: An uncle in Northumberland who is a hundred years old.
explanation.walkthrough: Northumberland is England's most north-easterly county, giving NE, which holds IE and C.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl or woman whose parent's brother is her uncle is a brother's or sister's daughter.

clue.text: Capital abroad, following one's nose

indicators.note: following places the capital after the other piece

parts.note: A is the indefinite article, one
Roma is Rome, the Italian capital, in its native Italian

explanation.surface: Someone travelling to a foreign capital by following their nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' asks for the capital's local name: Rome in Italian is ROMA, placed after A.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's nose is its smell, its bouquet or scent.

clue.text: Socialite and poet taking underground, westbound

indicators.note: taking signals the poet takes another word inside him

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

indicators.note: westbound, in an across clue, means travelling right to left

parts.note: the Tube is the London Underground

explanation.surface: A society girl and a poet ride the Underground heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'westbound' turns the Underground backwards, as an across entry reads west to east, and 'taking' puts the result inside the poet's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante is a young woman entering fashionable society, a socialite.

clue.text: Oriental festival on 1 st of November

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival

indicators.note: the first of November means its opening letter

explanation.surface: An Eastern festival held on the first day of November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins EASTER to N, the first letter of 'November'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental means of the East, the regions of Asia.

clue.text: Support in back or sides of shoe

parts.note: the end is the back or rear of something

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Support is needed at the back and sides of a shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: END + OR + SE, the first and last letters of 'shoe'; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to approve or back something publicly.
